title: Emotion: Definition & Theories
summary: Emotion defined and the four major theories: James–Lange, Cannon–Bard, Schachter–Singer (two-factor), and cognitive appraisal.
objectives: Describe James–Lange, Cannon–Bard, Schachter–Singer and cognitive appraisal theories.
revision: Emotion: definition and four theories — James–Lange (arousal → emotion), Cannon–Bard (simultaneous), Schachter–Singer (arousal + label), cognitive appraisal.

notes.t: A complex psychological state involving subjective experience, physiological arousal, expressive behaviour and cognitive appraisal.
Stimulus → physiological arousal → emotion; we feel afraid because we tremble, not the reverse.
Stimulus → simultaneous physiological arousal and emotional experience (thalamus relays to cortex and autonomic system at once).
Emotion = physiological arousal + cognitive label; arousal is undifferentiated until labelled.
Emotion follows how a person appraises/interprets a situation (primary appraisal: is this relevant? secondary appraisal: what can I do?).
UGC NET frequently asks to compare James–Lange, Cannon–Bard and Schachter–Singer theories.

mnemonics.title: JCSC
mnemonics.text: J — James–Lange (arousal → emotion), C — Cannon–Bard (simultaneous), S — Schachter–Singer (arousal + label), C — Cognitive appraisal (appraisal → emotion)

flashcards.a: Arousal → emotion (we tremble, therefore we feel afraid).
